todoAI — Master Task Table

Every task in numeric order, as of 2026-08-07 (branch-integration pass: all four branches merged into main 9d8b691; task 31 re-sized and briefed; score.ts NUL-byte fix landed). Status reflects the evidence base in docs/eval/, not summaries of it.

This file is the single source for per-task status. It moved into the repo on 2026-08-07; orientation_for_opus.md no longer carries a second copy of it. On conflict: this table wins on status; orientation wins on contracts, constraints, settled decisions, and ship gates; a per-task brief wins for its own task.

master_task_table.html is generated — do not hand-edit it. After changing this file run node scripts/gen-task-table.js.

Status key: ✅ Done · 🟡 Partial · ⬜ Undone · 🔴 Undone + gate/live bug

Model key: You (device/human judgment) · Fable (access ended) · Opus · Sonnet · Jason/Human

P in the Dep column = requires on-device (Phase B) verification. Desktop reasoning does not close these; a P task is not done until it has run on the S23 FE. Sequence headless work and device batches separately.

(There is no task 16 — retired and split into 23 + 24. Q1 sits between 5 and 6, where it ran. 39 is reserved and unused — held for an optional corpus→eval-harness step between 38 and 40. 41, 42 and 43 added 2026-08-07: 41 gates 31 after the dogfooding DB turned out to hold no real captures; 42 pins the closed-beta rung; 43 pins the open-beta and GA rungs so the pruning schedule can't be lost; 44 collects four alpha QoL items requested alongside 41 and kept separate from it deliberately; 45 audits the deviation backlog after task 24's dial change reached production without Jason ever being asked.)

"Done" and "merged" were different claims, and until 2026-08-07 this table only tracked the first. Tasks 35 and 36 were marked ✅ with reports and test counts — all true — while their work sat on an unmerged branch. The checked-out branch had no migration 006, no src/services/recurrence/, and no v2.4 spec. Since 36's whole content was a fix for a live scoring bug affecting every recurring task, an alpha built during those four days would have shipped the bug with the record insisting it was fixed.

New rule: a ✅ row names its branch until that branch is on main. All rows below are on main as of 9d8b691.

And main has never been test-verified. Not "re-confirm a green" — there has never been a green run on this tree. Run npx jest + npx tsc --noEmit + npx eslint . before building on it.

Brief rewritten 2026-08-07 — the original approach was wrong for this tree. 🔴 Do not file-copy the DB: (a) task 41's Phase 1 established there is no way to write a file from JS here — no RNFS, no FS TurboModule, op-sqlite gives paths but no write; and (b) a byte-copy of a live SQLite DB is unsafe anyway — with an open WAL it can capture a torn state, which would have been a latent integrity bug even with a filesystem API. 41Undone 🔴 Lossless local event capture Nothing gets discarded. Conversation logs (verbatim, both directions, incl. clarifying Q&A), task changes (user- vs model-made, field-level, with surface), task performance (episodes, outcomes, +5/hyperfocus, parks, crash recoveries). Ruled 2026-08-07: log everything in alpha, no exclusions or redaction — and build every stream to be removable independently. That's a settled decision (orientation §5), not a preference: streams separately scoped, each under a directory it owns, one module/one entry point, on-disk layout a written contract, no capture logic diffusing into instrumented code. 42 deletes one stream while keeping the rest, and must prove it. The crisis detector is untouched — only its logging is removable. Additions: 🔴 raw model I/O (composed prompt, raw completion before parsing, grammar, D10 rung, latency, tok/s), 🔴 validation failures with payload (LlmOutputValidationError currently drops it — that's why 37 cost a whole spike), scoring/planning snapshots incl. both reject sets, coaching lifecycle, crisis-gate firings + near-misses (task 21 has zero real data today), thermal/device conditions, app lifecycle. Design: out-of-band append-only JSONL on app-private storage — never in the product DB, must survive its corruption; synchronous writes (buffering loses exactly the events around a crash); capture failure never breaks the app but never silent either; correlation IDs + "v":1 on every record; redaction seams present but off. Acceptance test that matters: force-kill mid-episode loses nothing. Brief: docs/briefs/event_capture_task_41.md 24, 13, POpus + Jason (device)
42Undone 🔴 Crisis-stream teardown + consent for the surviving capture 🔴 HARD CLOSED-BETA GATE. Two jobs. (A) Teardown: the crisis-gate stream only is removed before beta — for a tester it's a record of their worst moments in a file, and no consent flow makes that worth it. Jason's own alpha crisis log is retained (it's task 21's only real evidence). The detector itself is untouched; only its logging goes. (B) Governance: the other streams ship and record beta testers, so consent (first-run, in 23's language, stating it never leaves the device), controls with real categories underneath, retention (⚠ data_retention — created in migration 001 with three policies, never written to or acted on; implement or retire it), and export/delete that provably reach both stores. Defaults are the real policy — recommend performance + model I/O on, raw transcripts off unless enabled, crisis stream nonexistent. Verified not asserted: grep the beta bundle for crisis symbols; fire the gate and confirm it still refers but logs nothing; toggle each control off and confirm the stream is empty; export-then-delete reaches both stores. Private archive: retained logs, corpus text and the crisis log live outside the repo — the repo travels, and retained-forever + committed-to-git means a verbatim record of Jason's life ships with the source. Also builds the egress pipeline: ruled 2026-08-07, nothing leaves a tester's device un-anonymized — anonymization runs at the source, before export, as a pipeline distinct from capture (consuming 41's redaction seams). Closed beta is the last rung where free-text egress is defensible, and only because the volume permits per-item review. Also owes: the conversation_summary comment correction and constraint #7's clause (local capture ≠ telemetry; the distinction is transmission). Review with task 21. Brief: docs/briefs/privacy_consent_task_42.md 41, 21Opus implements
43Undone Capture ladder — open-beta and GA pruning 🔴 Gates OPEN BETA, then GA (42 owns the closed-beta rung). Ruled 2026-08-07: logging will be pruned/dropped as we move from closed beta to open beta to general release. The mechanism, not a mood: the closed-beta safeguard is human review of a small volume from known people — and that does not scale, and fails silently. The stream must narrow exactly where the protection stops being real. Open beta: free-text conversation capture is dropped; structured streams (performance, outcomes, timings, model-I/O metadata, thermal, errors) survive, because they carry 17/19/20's signal with almost none of the exposure. GA: minimal or nothing. Prune by dropping, not disabling. Anonymization is best-effort on free text and "anonymized" never means "safe to publish" — the real risk is re-identification by combination, since a task list is close to a fingerprint even fully scrubbed. That asymmetry (structured anonymizes completely, free text doesn't) is what makes the ladder principled rather than an arbitrary line. ⚠ See the corpus-window consequence in the frontier section. Brief: docs/briefs/capture_ladder_task_43.md 42Opus implements; Jason rules each rung
44Undone Personal-use QoL pass Four alpha QoL items, numbered apart from 41 deliberately (41 is critical-path with a closing corpus window; this is product UI). Batch onto 41's device session. All product questions RULED 2026-08-07 — build to them: (a) a task blocked by other tasks disables both quick-start and self-complete (dependency-blocked and R7-held parents; disabled with a visible reason, not hidden); (b) self-completed tasks are excluded from completion-time calculations; (c) quick-start runs the full check-in — a normal session that's one task long; (d) if any check-in condition would have filtered the task out (including missing tools) → warning screen naming the condition, with a back-out button; proceed allowed, but informed; (e) logs distinguish quick-start vs normal sessions. Items: (1) model warm-up on coaching-screen open — modelHost.ts already has ensure() + phase(), so it's when ensure() is called; makes constraint #3 safer, not weaker. (2) Timer dial — deferred to the designed pass; in this task only fix the false code comment (WorkScreen.tsx cites "per the task brief" for a bar the brief never mentions → task 45). (3) Quick-start, reusing the real src/planning/ predicates for the warning so it can't drift from the filter it mirrors. (4) Self-complete — reuse completeTask() (already branches per constraint #7, runs 33's fold + 36's advance); interactions row with explicit null runtime fields, counts for completion/neglect, excluded from duration learning. ⚠ Candidate first writer for completion_count/success_rate — record the convention so task 17 inherits it. RULED 2026-08-07: session origin goes in sessions.origin (planned|quickstart) as well as the capture logs — migration 007 / schema 2.8.0, one writer in sessionController.startSession, NULL meaning the distinction didn't exist yet. Why, so nobody reads it as a redundant duplicate: capture is deletable by design (removable streams, consent-gated at 42, pruned by 43) and a permanent consumer must not depend on an ephemeral store — the general rule being anything the app reasons about itself with belongs in the DB; capture is for diagnosis and corpus. Quick-start also bypasses runSelectionBoundary, so it's a confounder not a label: its outcome says nothing about whether the ranker chose well, and pooling it credits the scorer for the user's own pick. And it can't be backfilled — deferring until 17 exists destroys the record for every session in the gap. Scope: record it; how 17 consumes it is 17's call. Brief: docs/briefs/personal_qol_task_44.md 24, PSonnet

Where the frontier is — two threads, and they don't compete

🔴 The corpus collection window is finite, and that reprices everything below. The capture ladder (43) drops free-text conversation capture at open beta — permanently ending the supply of real conversational input that 31's corpus, 38's training data and 40's held-out eval all depend on. The corpus is built during alpha and closed beta, or it is largely not built at all, and every future LoRA iteration and every re-run of the bake-off draws on a corpus whose window has already shut. This is an argument for starting 41 now rather than after the beta-hardening work, and for closed beta being generous with free-text capture while consent and review are still real protections. It is not an argument for extending the window — the mechanism in 43 doesn't bend.

Thread 1 — the strategic one (the model-migration decision). Now 41 → 31 → 38 → 40, then Jason's call. Task 41 is the new front of the chain and it's the move that can happen today: once capture is on, the corpus accumulates while you do everything else, which is the only input on the board that grows without effort. 31's interview and reconstruction work runs in parallel with the capture window rather than waiting on it.

Thread 2 — the tree, then beta hardening. In order: (a) run the three checks on main; (b) push main to GitHub; (c) task 37, the live grammar bug, before any alpha capture or the bake-off; then 14 / 15 / 17 / 21 / 32 and the designed visual pass.

Beta gates: the designed/polished pass (24, consuming 23's tokens), 21 (crisis, human), 42 (privacy/consent — pinned here for the same reason as 21, and reviewed with it), 30 (device envelope, Jason), 20 (real eval numbers), 32's device residue. General: 29 only, re-scoped to a Vulkan-throughput question.
